chapter: Hollywood, Ken Murray and the Penguin years
title: Doubling at the Trocadero and the agency feud over the Blackouts
summary: He doubled at the Trocadero with Jack McVea in the band; the Hollywood office opposed him but Billy Shaw won.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: You didn't do any recording out on the coast at all, did you?
I didn't do any recording at all.
Aside from Billy Berg's did you do anything--not Billy Berg, aside from Ken Murray's thing--after you came out of Ken Murray's where did you go then?
While I was in Ken Murray's Blackouts, I was also doubling at the Trocadara (phonetic spelling).
Jack McVea's in this band too now?
Yeah, Jack McVea was in the band, the guy that wrote, "Open the Door, Richard."
Yeah, but that was after he left you.
After he left me; right.
He was pretty successful out there.
He still is doing pretty good.
Didn't they try to get you a record contract?
I often wondered why they didn't, but they had a feud going on. The Hollywood office wanted one of their bands to go with the Blackouts; they didn't want me to go in.
They didn't want you to go in the Blackouts?
No.
I could understand,

because that would actually bury you, in a way. The Hollywood office didn't, but the New York office did, with Billy Shaw. So, I wanted to go in there and Billy Shaw called up out there and said, I want that band in there and they put me in there.
Do you think it did you--
It did me a world of good.
It did you a world of good?
Yeah. The only thing--
